exchanges.subject: Delgado: Lone Star at 80%. Your call on liability
exchanges.body:
Craig's offering 80% ($5,940). He hasn't mentioned the dash cam. Do we take it or push? If we take it, Rosa gets
80% of her deductible back. Sandra

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Sandra, I'd reject the 80%. Liability is 100% theirs: the dash cam shows Rosa stopped at a red light on Loop 363 for about 6 seconds before Pope hit her, and the CR-3 cites Pope for failure to control speed. Nothing supports a sudden stop on a yellow. Please counter at the full $7,425.00, which includes Rosa's $500 deductible, and send Craig the clip. If they won't move, let's file intercompany arbitration. If we took 80%, Rosa would get back only $400 of her deductible, and I don't think the facts justify that.

Liability: clear (insured ran the stop sign at FM 2305 and Old Waco Rd; cited). Injuries: right shoulder partial rotator cuff tear, arthroscopic repair 11/12/2025, 16 weeks PT. exchanges.body: That's fine. What do I need to do?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Sign the owner-retained salvage form I'll email you this morning and send me the title. Please have the truck moved from Bell County Towing this week; we'll pay their storage through Friday. We pay within five business days after we receive the signed form and title.

exchanges.author: c_graves
exchanges.body: Okay. I'll get it done.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Inbound 11/4 09:10. Insured elects to keep the Ranger (owner-retained salvage). Settlement: ACV $6,880 - $500 deductible - $1,310 Copart salvage bid = $5,070. Explained salvage title and that it must be repaired and re-titled before driving. Owner-retained form to be emailed today; title to follow. Storage at Bell County Towing paid through Fri 11/6; insured to move the truck. Payment within 5 business days of signed form and title. Copart pickup to be cancelled.

exchanges.author: c_benavides
exchanges.body: This is Luis Benavides. I got your letter. Thirty percent my fault? That lady wasn't even looking at me. And what are Mr. Fry's policy limits? I want to see what he told you, too.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: I understand you disagree, Mr. Benavides. We based the percentage on the police report, which estimated your speed at forty-eight in a thirty-five, and on an independent witness who described the same thing. If you have anything that shows otherwise, like dash camera video or another witness, send it to me and I'll review it.

exchanges.author: c_benavides
exchanges.body: I don't have video. So what are his limits? I have a right to know who I'm dealing with.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: I can't share our insured's policy information or his statement without his written consent. What I can tell you is that his coverage is enough for your damages, so the limit doesn't change what we've offered.

exchanges.author: c_benavides
exchanges.body: Fine. I'll think about it and call you.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Inbound 11/4 11:45. Claimant disputes 30% fault. Explained basis (CR-3 estimated 48 in a 35; independent witness). Invited any new evidence; he has no video. He asked for the insured's limits and statement: declined without the insured's written consent; told him coverage is sufficient for his damages. He will consider the $6,522.60 offer and call back.

exchanges.author: c_glen
exchanges.body: Yeah, Glen Ostrowski, claim for my Altima from the hail last week. When am I getting paid? I sent you the photos already.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks for calling, Mr. Ostrowski. I've got your photos. The next step is an in-person inspection at our drive-in center in Temple; could you bring the car in this Friday or Monday?

exchanges.author: c_glen
exchanges.body: Why do you need to see it? The photos show the dents.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: We inspect most hail claims in person to write an accurate estimate. It takes about twenty minutes. Monday at ten?

exchanges.author: c_hughes
exchanges.body: Hi, Darnell Hughes. I got your letter about the title for my Altima. I've looked everywhere. I think it was in the glove box when the car was stolen.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: That happens a lot, Mr. Hughes. You can get a certified copy from TxDMV with Form VTR-34. It's two dollars by mail, or five dollars and forty-five cents in person at a TxDMV Regional Service Center. When you have it, sign it as the seller and mail it to me with the power of attorney.

exchanges.author: c_hughes
exchanges.body: Can't you just do it without me?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: If we don't have it by November 13th, we can apply for a title in our name, since we've now sent you two written requests, but that takes longer. Either way, your settlement is already paid; this just completes the transfer.

exchanges.author: c_hughes
exchanges.body: Okay, I'll mail the form this week.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Inbound 11/4 16:35. Insured believes the title was in the glove box when stolen. Explained certified copy via TxDMV Form VTR-34 ($2 by mail; $5.45 in person at a Regional Service Center), to be signed over with the POA. Told him we may apply for a title in our name after 11/13 (two written requests sent: 10/1 and 11/3). He will mail the VTR-34 this week.

Rental: the policy's transportation expense coverage pays up to $30 a day, $900 maximum, beginning 24 hours after the loss. Mr. Jennings chose a full-size car at $33.50 a day (RA 54877, 10/6 to 11/3, 28 days, $938.00). We pay 28 x $30.00 = $840.00, under the $900 maximum; the $98.00 balance is the rate above $30 a day. The time to repair was driven by the parts backorder, not by claim handling; every statutory step was met.

documents.title: LR-26-117922 (Mendez): witness statement summary, Ruben Mendez

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# LR-26-117922: witness statement (Ruben Mendez), by phone 11/4 14:30, recorded with permission

Relationship: claimant's cousin. Says he was driving behind the claimant, northbound on S General Bruce Dr at Central Ave, 9/14 about 19:30; says the claimant's light was green and our insured turned left in front of him.
Conflicts: the claimant's own recorded statement (9/16) says he was alone at the light with no cars behind him and that his cousin arrived after the crash. The CR-3 lists no witnesses; the officer's diagram and our insured's statement put the claimant entering on red. Ruben could not say what color the light was for our insured or where his own car stopped.
Assessment: an interested witness whose position conflicts with the claimant's earlier account; does not outweigh the CR-3 and the insured's statement. Recommend maintaining the denial, with the reasons in writing, and inviting any other evidence (traffic camera, other witnesses).
